brief.scope:
Fix-round review of PR #242 (lane/session-20260916-d, head e0e0b732), fresh round after the first (records 20260916T075500Z-review-grok-c7a708, 20260916T075518Z-review-codex-c22c2d), whose 11 accepted findings this head answers in fix commit 65967fa8, one Finding/Verified pair per finding: the server renamed to coordination, placement engine none, the seam settled against the core at 05b8aebe on lane/session-20260916-c via the CORE table with reader and writer store handles, refusals on resources/read as JSON-RPC error objects carrying the wire line, an explicit tool-to-verb table.
Check each fix against its finding: is any accepted finding only partly fixed; do the 11 new test cases pin the fixed behaviour itself, not just the words used to describe it.

caps.turns_note: codex offers no turn-cap flag (measured 2026-09-12: its --help names none); caps.turns is recorded, the wall cap governs

findings.claim: X#1's core-composition failure is only partly fixed. Selecting CORE and passing reader/writer handles is correct, but call() still forwards only the advertised arguments. At 05b8aebe, ten projected mutations require an additional keyword-only agent, core_show requires target rather than assignment, and generation gates call .isdigit() although this server passes JSON integers. Direct composition measured coord_brief succeeding while coord_draft raised missing agent, coord_show raised unexpected assignment, and integer generation raised AttributeError. Because _dispatch catches only Refusal, these valid calls terminate without a JSON-RPC response. The mock hides this by accepting **arguments and omitting the core's required agent parameter, so the new seam tests do not pin the delivered core behavior.
findings.reproduce: git -C /home/scientdb/projects/uscient/agentscient show 05b8aebe:ops/conductor/tools/coordination.py | rg -n '^def core_(draft|show|resolve)|^def require_generation' && nl -ba ops/conductor/tools/coordination_mcp.py | sed -n '448,460p'

findings.claim: G#3's participant-row check does not understand the real core result. core_participants at 05b8aebe returns {"participants":[...]}; each participant_dict has participant="PT-n" and an integer id. _row_named accepts only a top-level list/tuple and compares row['id'] to the PT-n string, so an existing participant is always reported absent. The clean-neighbor test plants a bare list with id="PT-7", a shape the core never returns, and therefore certifies the mock rather than the fixed behavior.

X#3's bounds are still descriptions rather than the promised runtime behavior. Adding an optional cursor input does not page results or return a next cursor, and the 05b8aebe assignments/inbox/outstanding verbs do not accept cursor, so supplying the advertised field raises TypeError. The response bound is applied only to the payload before tools/call duplicates it into content and structuredContent; a 12,013-byte accepted payload produces a 24,140-byte response despite the declared 16,384-byte whole-response bound. The new tests inspect the schema word cursor and an already-oversized payload, so neither defect is pinned.
findings.reproduce: PYTHONPATH=ops/conductor/tools python3 -B -c "import coordination_mcp as m; p={'rows':['x'*12000]}; b=m.bounded(p); r=m._result(1,{'content':[{'type':'text','text':m.canonical(b)}],'structuredContent':b,'isError':False}); print(len(m.canonical(p).encode()),len(m.canonical(r).encode()),m.RESPONSE_BYTES)"

findings.claim: X#4's method-specific validation is only partly implemented. initialize now rejects a non-string protocolVersion, but still accepts malformed capabilities/clientInfo and unknown members; tools/list and resources/list still accept arbitrary parameters. The added tests cover only the single protocolVersion example and the explicit ruling that ping permits extras, leaving the rest of the accepted finding unpinned.
findings.reproduce: PYTHONPATH=ops/conductor/tools python3 -B -c "import coordination_mcp as m; cases=[{'jsonrpc':'2.0','id':1,'method':'initialize','params':{'protocolVersion':'2025-06-18','capabilities':[],'clientInfo':'bad','bogus':1}},{'jsonrpc':'2.0','id':2,'method':'tools/list','params':{'bogus':1}},{'jsonrpc':'2.0','id':3,'method':'resources/list','params':{'bogus':1}}]; print([m._dispatch(None,c) for c in cases])"

findings.claim: G#4/X#6 remains internally contradictory. The new paragraph gives the implemented order—named authority, capability, argument shape, binding—but the preceding projection description still says arguments, binding, then capability. The new test asserts only the remedy sentence and does not exercise precedence with both a forbidden authority key and a missing capability, so it cannot catch this surviving contract conflict.

The G#5/X#5 and 05b8aebe documentation fixes are incomplete. Section 2.2 still promises class identity for a missing participant row although the core emits participant; section 2.4 still says an absent binding makes mutations refuse identity although the implementation and registry emit session; section 4 says identity is never emitted. The contract header and test header still say the seam is settled at 537f3a35, while section 7 says 05b8aebe, and section 9 still describes the superseded resolve()/return_ lookup and missing explicit-session bind even though 05b8aebe provides bound_participant, CORE and core_bind_for. The accepted fixes therefore leave the declared coupling and refusal contract non-stationary.
